title: Primitive Instance cardinality is encoded in the name of the Instance Configuration Document
content:
Pattern's Genesis Primitives each hold a document titled "Single Instance Configuration Document" — for Agent Creation (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.3.1), Prime Transformation (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.3.1) and the Agent Token (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.2.1). The Executor Accord Primitive, which stays open, instead holds an "Ozone Instance Configuration Document" (A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.2.1) — named after the instance rather than its cardinality.

The convention makes a structural fact legible at the heading level. "Single" is a claim about the Primitive, not just about the current count: it asserts that no second instance is possible, consistent with the sealed In Progress Invocations Directories. A named instance implies the opposite — that a sibling could be added and would need its own name to be distinguishable.

The practical value is that a reader navigating the tree learns the cardinality contract before opening the document, and any future edit that adds a second instance under a "Single" heading is immediately visible as a contradiction rather than a quiet insertion.

The accompanying "Instance Configuration Document Location" pointers (e.g. A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.1.3.1) exist because the directory and the document live in different subtrees — the cost of encoding state as location is that cross-links must be maintained.
description: One-shot Primitives use a 'Single Instance Configuration Document'; repeatable ones give each Instance a proper name, so a reader can tell from the heading whether sibling Instances can exist.
